text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Seventeen million people are to vote on Thursday to elect 380-seat National Assembly.
- The general election is a significant stage for political development in Algeria, says the U.S. administration.
- Party leaders spearheaded 19-day-long poll campaigning despite wave of attacks.
- Secular Socialist Forces Front (FFS) bet on supporters of the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) to back FFS candidates for the parliamentary election.
- The voters will choose on Thursday between realism and opportunism.

- Oil Minister Amar Makhloufi says during a visit to Spain that gas pipeline linking Algeria's Hassi R'mel gas field to Europe via Morocco and Spain offers more prospects for cooperation between Algeria and Spain.
- President Liamine Zeroual vows that Thursday's election will take place in total calm.
- Algerian voters will turn out in large numbers to cast ballots on Thursday, Zeroual says.
